question: Does every inch of height add to your pay?
answer: Four big US and UK studies found each inch of height was worth about $789 a year, so a 6′0″ person averages about $5,523 more a year than a 5′5″ colleague. Others rate tall people higher, across 45 studies. For men, height at 16 seems to predict adult pay, not later growth.
move: For men, the inches that pay may be those you had at 16, not now.

web.label: Interactive card asking whether each inch of height adds to pay. It compares a 6′0″ person with a 5′5″ colleague, showing about $5,523 a year more on average and $166,000 over 30 years. A draggable pencil marks height on a door frame.
